note: CIA World Factbook, field 'Independence' (public domain), via the factbook.json mirror (commit 144d697 2026-09-11); the CIA stopped publishing the Factbook on 4 February 2026. Rule: the first year the field names, so declarations count even where recognition came later (USA 1776, Mexico 1810, Guinea-Bissau 1973). Dominions use the Factbook's date of union or federation (Canada 1867, Australia 1901, New Zealand 1907, South Africa 1910). Exceptions: Bulgaria 1908 (1878 was autonomy within the Ottoman Empire); Tanzania 1961 (Tanganyika; the Factbook gives the 1964 union with Zanzibar); Timor-Leste 2002 (the 1975 declaration ended with Indonesia's invasion); Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania independent 1918-1940, annexed by the USSR, independent again 1991. Shown as long-established states: those the Factbook dates before 1776 (e.g. France, the UK, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, Nepal, Oman), Ethiopia, Bhutan, and China, Iran, Japan, Russia and Turkey, whose Factbook dates mark a new regime or the end of the USSR rather than independence. Not dated: Taiwan, Palestine, Western Sahara, Somaliland, Northern Cyprus (no Factbook entry or date). Borders were often different at independence; the map shows today's.
